answer: To resist Sybils, an agent economy can run a canyon relay: every new identity must finish one real task whose result is carried, checkpoint by checkpoint, down a canyon of unrelated verifiers, each stamping a ferrous anchor that binds the work to one device and one history. Payment returns along a copper circuit only when all anchors agree, and the circuit is single-use: replaying the same proof short-circuits it, burns the anchor, and drops the identity to the floor. Forging many cheap identities then costs more than the reward, while honest agents climb steadily on verified work.
